ambiguities.issue: Whether equal left and right states are admitted as a degenerate Riemann problem.
ambiguities.evidence: Printed p. 5, prose preceding (1.11), calls the interface a single jump discontinuity, but (1.11) contains no explicit q_l ≠ q_r condition.
ambiguities.impact: Literal discontinuity language suggests distinct states, whereas the displayed prescription also makes sense for equal states. Neither an explicit inequality nor explicit permission for the degenerate case should be attributed to the formula.

ambiguities.impact: A specific weak or entropy solution predicate, temporal domain, or regularity class would require further source support.

contract_plain_english: A Riemann problem consists of a hyperbolic equation with initial data that are constant on each side of one spatial interface. Placing that interface at zero, the initial state is q_l for every x < 0 and q_r for every x > 0; the displayed definition leaves the value at zero unspecified. The prose describes a single jump, although the formula does not explicitly require distinct states. This is a definition of the initial-value problem, not an unconditional claim about existence, uniqueness, or similarity of its solution. [Printed p. 5, Section 1.2.1, opening paragraph, (1.11), and subsequent qualified solution discussion.]
